q: What are the five sections of an agent file?
explanation: The agent file is a document with ROLE (who it is), RULES (tone, format, privacy red lines), MEMORY (context and templates), OUTPUT (exact format) and CHECKS (verification questions).

q: Which way of starting a run does the course teach as its main method?
options: Waiting for the platform to start the run by itself
Running it yourself at a fixed time, prompted by a phone reminder
Hiring a person to run the prompts
Leaving the chat open all day
explanation: Running the agent yourself is free and works on any phone with internet access, so it is the course method. Scheduled features (ChatGPT Tasks, Gemini scheduled actions) are optional extras, and whether they are free varies.

q: What does 'chaining two steps' mean in an agent run?
options: Sending the same prompt to two different apps
One run that first extracts the action points, then drafts the report
Asking two people to check the work
explanation: Chaining means one run does several steps in order: first extract, then draft. It is your first multi-step agent run.

q: Why does the CHECKS section belong inside the agent file?
options: To make the file look longer
So every run flags sources, doubts and numbers for you to check
To charge the user for each check
explanation: The Day 2 verification questions are built into the agent itself: name sources, flag uncertainty, list every number to check. Quality control is built into the design from the start.
